method: 5 finder dimensions x adversarial verification (10 agents)

confirmed.title: Em-dash "—" placeholder bypasses the canonical "--" no-value token at ~10 production render sites
confirmed.evidence: House rule: values are numeral-or-"--", and the canonical token exists (AtriaMetricConfidencePresentation.swift:76 `static let noValue = "--"`; ~240 sites use "--"). But ~10 user-visible renders use em-dash instead — even mixed inside the SAME struct: AtriaHomeView.swift:8350 `var batteryText: String { batteryLevel >= 0 ? "\(batteryLevel)%" : "—" }` vs line 8377 `guard batteryLevel >= 0 else { return "--" }` (batteryHeaderChargeText). Other production sites: AtriaHistorySection.swift:561 `Text(day.strain.map { "\(AtriaMetricFormat.strain($0)) strain" } ?? "—")`, :1419 `value: day.recovery.map { "\($0)%" } ?? "—"`, :1431 `value: day.rhrInt.map { "\($0) bpm" } ?? "—"`; AtriaBreathworkSession.swift:377 `Text("—")` (big 38pt stress value); AtriaStressDetailView.swift:651 `score?.formatted(...) ?? "—"`; Insights.swift:553 `Text(baseline.restingInt.map { "\($0)" } ?? "—")`; Sessions.swift:37577-37579 `resting = metricsComplete ? "\(session.resting)" : "—"` (rendered via stat("Resting", summary.resting) at :37490); AtriaVitalsCollectionSections.swift:3467 battery tile `: "—"`. AtriaOverviewSections.swift:11434 even has to special-case both glyphs: `if v.isEmpty || v == "—" || v == "--" { return true }` — evidence the split is a known hazard.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Replace every user-visible "—" fallback with AtriaMetricConfidencePresentation.noValue ("--") so the not-computable token is one glyph app-wide; keep "—" only for BLE-internal debug strings (AtriaBLEManager dbg* fields).
confirmed.why: All cited sites verified as production-reachable renders (none inside #if DEBUG or previews: AtriaHistorySection's DEBUG block spans 898-947, outside lines 561/1419/1431; Breathwork's DEBUG block closes at 219, before Text("—") at 377). The canonical token exists (AtriaMetricConfidencePresentation.swift:76 noValue = "--"; 219 literal "--" sites vs 22 "—" sites). The split occurs inside a single struct (AtriaHomeView.swift:8350 batteryText "—" vs 8377 batteryHeaderChargeText "--"), and batteryText renders on-screen at AtriaOverviewSections.swift:4988 and AtriaStrapScreen.swift:51. AtriaOverviewSections.swift:11434 special-casing both glyphs proves the hazard is real, and no comment or doc justifies the em-dash as deliberate.

confirmed.title: Patterns glance chip renders a placeholder for a computable zero, while its sibling chip renders "0d"
confirmed.evidence: AtriaOverviewSections.swift:14841-14847, same HStack: `glanceChip(title: "Logged", value: taggedDays > 0 ? "\(taggedDays)d" : "0d", ...)` then `glanceChip(title: "Patterns", value: patternCount > 0 ? "\(patternCount)" : "—", ...)`. Zero detected patterns is a computed result, not an unavailable one — the house rule says "--" (let alone "—") is ONLY for not-computable. The adjacent chip proves the intended treatment ("0d"), so a user sees "Logged 3d" next to "Patterns —" and reads the journal-pattern scan as broken/unmeasured when it actually ran and found zero.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Render "0" when patternCount == 0 (mirroring the Logged chip), reserving the no-value token for the state where pattern analysis hasn't run (e.g. not enough tagged days).
confirmed.why: Verified: AtriaOverviewSections.swift:14846 renders "—" when patternCount == 0, in the same HStack as the Logged chip's "0d" (14841-14843). patternCount (14762) is summaries.filter { $0.impactDelta != nil }.count — always computable. Reachable in production via the Overview "Impacts" card (AtriaOverviewBehaviorJournalContent:14654 → glance board at 14692), shown whenever summaries or behaviorImpacts are non-empty, so a wearer with tagged days but no confirmed patterns hits it. No nearby comment or doc justifies it. Even under the charitable reading that all-nil impactDelta means "still building" (a not-computable state), the site would still be wrong — it uses the non-canonical "—" glyph instead of "--".

confirmed.title: Customize-sheet preview fabricates metric numerals ("72" live HR, "64%", "58" RHR, "31" bio age) in a production sheet with no sample-data label
confirmed.evidence: AtriaCustomizePreview is production code (no #if DEBUG), presented from AtriaHomeView.swift:1433 via the Customize Today sheet (embedded at AtriaCustomizeSheet.swift:64). It renders invented measurements: line 394 `previewCard(title: "Live", value: "72", icon: "heart.fill", ...)`, line 421 sleep `value: "7:42"`, line 430 recovery `value: "64%"`, line 439 strain `value: "8.4"`, plus sampleValue(for:) at lines 494-518 (`case .hrv: return "48 ms"`, `case .rhr: return "58"`, `case .vo2max: return "42"`, `case .bioAge: return "31"`, etc.). Nothing on screen marks these as example values — the only hint is `accessibilitySummary: "Customize preview"` (VoiceOver-only). The function itself is honesty-aware (`case .bloodOxygen, .bodyTemp: return "--"` for metrics the strap can't measure), yet a wearer whose real recovery is nil sees a confident "64%" and "72" bpm inside the app, violating never-fabricate.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Either feed the preview the wearer's real current values (falling back to "--" per metric), or stamp a visible "Example values" caption on the preview card so the fabricated numerals cannot be read as measurements.
confirmed.why: Verified: AtriaCustomizeSheet.swift contains zero #if DEBUG; AtriaCustomizePreview (line 369) is embedded in an untitled Form Section at line 64-66 of the production Customize Today sheet. Hardcoded numerals confirmed: previewCard "72" (394), tri-ring "7:42"/"64%"/"8.4" (421/430/439), sampleValue "58"/"31"/"42"/"48 ms" (494-518). The only sample marking is the VoiceOver-only accessibilitySummary "Customize preview" (382) — nothing visual. The function's own honesty-awareness ("--" for bloodOxygen/bodyTemp) confirms authors knew the honesty rules applied here. The handoff doc (HANDOFF_2026-08-03, sec 15.58) records the live preview shipping but documents no decision that unlabeled fabricated values are acceptable, so it stands as a never-fabricate violation. Mitigating context (mockup scaled 0.60, hit-testing disabled, inside a layout-customization form) softens severity but does not refute the claim.

confirmed.title: Developer mode has no compile-time DEBUG barrier and self-persists for 7 days, violating the codebase's own shipped-binary standard
confirmed.evidence: AtriaDeveloperMode.swift has zero `#if DEBUG` (verified: grep count 0). Lines 18-26: `if arguments.contains(launchArgument) { defaults.set(true, forKey: defaultsKey); defaults.set(now.addingTimeInterval(leaseDuration), ...); return true }` — `--atria-developer-mode` works in a Release binary and then persists via UserDefaults for `leaseDuration = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60`. Consumers in Release: AtriaHomeView.swift:1633-1635 exposes the developer "Research & Validation" settings section (`researchValidationContent: developerModeEnabled ? ...`), and ContentView.swift:42-43 + Sessions.swift:17497-17501 let `--atria-complete-onboarding` mark onboarding complete with an unconfigured profile. The codebase's own standard is explicit at Sessions.swift:15886-15889: "a shipped binary must have a compile-time barrier here too, not just the launch-argument gate" — and every UI fixture obeys it; this gate does not.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Wrap AtriaDeveloperMode.isEnabled's argument/defaults path in #if DEBUG (returning false in Release), matching the compile-time barrier standard already applied to every --atria-ui-fixture site; keep the 7-day lease for DEBUG builds only.
confirmed.why: Verified: AtriaDeveloperMode.swift has zero #if DEBUG; lines 21-24 set the defaults flag plus a 7-day expiry (leaseDuration = 7*24*60*60) on any launch carrying --atria-developer-mode, in any build configuration, and isEnabled then returns true argument-free for 7 days. Release consumers confirmed: AtriaHomeView.swift:995/1633 (Research & Validation settings section), ContentView.swift:42-43 and Sessions.swift:17497-17500 (onboarding skip with unconfigured profile). The codebase's own standard is explicit at Sessions.swift:15886-15889 ("a shipped binary must have a compile-time barrier here too, not just the launch-argument gate") and the sibling fixtures obey it. The in-file comment (lines 15-17) documents why the lease persists across CoreBluetooth restores, but not the absence of a Release barrier — so it is not a documented decision covering the violation. Caveat consistent with its low grade: triggering requires launch-arg injection via developer tooling, not a plain App Store tap, but this app's real distribution channel is dev-install with launch args, where the path is genuinely exercised.

confirmed.title: Hardcoded 60 bpm resting-HR default silently shapes historical and relaunch-recovery strain/zone numbers without any provenance or confidence downgrade
confirmed.evidence: Three historical-projection sites substitute a fabricated resting HR when none is known: AtriaBLEManager.swift:12292 `let restingHeartRate = restingHR ?? 60` (also :31119, :33039), feeding `AtriaHistoricalConsumerProjectionConfiguration.production(restingHeartRate:...)`, whose activity/workout Confidence enum (AtriaHistoricalActivityProjection.swift:640-646) is coverage-based only — the "default RHR used" fact is dropped, so drained history renders strain/elevated-threshold numerals computed from an invented 60 bpm with full confidence. Same pattern at AtriaWorkoutRuntime.swift:398-400: `rest: intent.calculationContext?.restingHeartRate ?? store.baseline.restingInt ?? 60` when confirming a recovered live workout. Contrast the widget path, which handles this honestly: WidgetSnapshot.swift:522-527 passes `hasRestingHeartRateEvidence: rest != nil` into strainConfidence so the same `rest ?? 60` is downgraded. New wearer with no baseline + history drain = days of confidently-rendered strain built on the literal 60.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Thread a hasRestingHeartRateEvidence flag (as WidgetSnapshot already does) into the historical projection configuration and the workout-confirm path so strain derived from the 60 bpm default surfaces with a downgraded/estimate confidence, or defer projection until a real resting baseline exists.
confirmed.why: Verified end-to-end: the three AtriaBLEManager sites (12292, 31119, 33039) each read the bare member property (line 1180: var restingHR: Int? { sessionMinHeartRate } — nil for a fresh wearer or pre-HR relaunch; no shadowing parameter in the enclosing private funcs) and feed AtriaHistoricalConsumerProjectionConfiguration.production, whose restingHeartRate drives elevated/vigorous thresholds (AtriaHistoricalActivityProjection.swift:571-572, 629; AtriaHistoricalSleepWorkoutProjections.swift:959-960). The projection's Confidence enum (AtriaHistoricalActivityProjection.swift:640-647) is purely count/coverage-based — the default-RHR fact is dropped. AtriaWorkoutRuntime.swift:398-400 confirms recovered live workouts with rest ?? 60. The widget contrast is real: WidgetSnapshot.swift:522 passes hasRestingHeartRateEvidence: rest != nil, downgrading strainConfidence to "learning" (AtriaHomeView.swift:10065) even while computing with rest ?? 60. The (25...150) validation guard passes 60 unchallenged, and no doc records the default as a deliberate decision. All paths are production (no DEBUG gating).

confirmed.title: Expanded chart redraws the line ACROSS day gaps that the compact metric-detail chart honestly breaks
confirmed.evidence: AtriaExpandedChart.swift:455-459 draws the current series as ONE continuous line: `LineMark(x: .value("Day", point.day, unit: .day), y: .value(title, point.value), series: .value("Series", "current")).interpolationMethod(.linear)` — a single fixed series id for every point, no gap split (the AreaMark at 448-453 and the prior overlay at 294-301 share the defect). The house mechanism exists and is documented as shared: AtriaStrainRecoveryComboChart.swift:161-166 `/// Split into contiguous day-runs so a charted line BREAKS at day gaps ... Shared by the combo and the metric detail charts`, and the compact chart this screen expands FROM uses it — AtriaOverviewSections.swift:10831-10833 `ForEach(points.contiguousDayRuns(), id: \.point.day) { entry in LineMark(... series: .value("Series", "current-\(entry.runID)"))`. Failure: HRV over a month with a 5-night wear gap — the compact chart shows two runs with an honest blank; tap Expand and the full-screen chart draws a straight segment bridging the same 5 days, implying readings that never existed. Violates the "lines break at day gaps" rule on the app's flagship exploration surface.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In currentSeriesMarks (.line case) iterate `points.contiguousDayRuns()` and use `series: .value("Series", "current-\(entry.runID)")`; do the same for the priorPoints compare overlay and the overlay series (rescaledOverlayPoints preserves days, so runs survive rescaling).
confirmed.why: AtriaExpandedChart.swift:455-459 draws one fixed 'current' series with .linear interpolation (AreaMark 448-453 and prior overlay 294-301 share it); no contiguousDayRuns() split. Reachable from two production fullScreenCover paths (AtriaOverviewSections.swift:8891, AtriaTrendChart.swift:214). The shared mechanism exists (AtriaStrainRecoveryComboChart.swift:160-182), is documented as shared, and IS used by the compact chart the user expands from (AtriaOverviewSections.swift:10831-10833). No comment or doc claims bridging is deliberate here. Survives all three refutation tests.

confirmed.title: Trends-card expanded chart never receives prior-period data — Compare and Edit-chart falsely claim no history exists
confirmed.evidence: AtriaTrendChart.swift:215-220 opens the shared expanded chart with `AtriaExpandedChartView(title: "\(metric.shortLabel) trend", unit: expandedUnit, tint: metric.tint, points: expandedChartPoints, events: events, onDismiss: ...)` — no `priorPoints`, no `overlays`, no `comparisonPeriodNoun`. AtriaExpandedChart.swift:508-512 then computes `compareAvailability` with `previousPeriodCount: priorPoints.count` = 0, so every compare mode is disabled and the sheet shows "Not enough saved history before this window yet" / "Nothing to compare against yet" (AtriaGraphGrammar.swift:98-99, 373). But the SAME compact card computed and is DRAWING that prior series: prepareSeries builds the time-shifted ghost (AtriaTrendChart.swift:292-295) and renders it as a dashed line when `showGhost` (444-457, gate 562-564 — the identical `max(3, count/2)` evidence rule compare uses). So the user sees a dashed prior-period line on the card, expands it, taps Compare, and is told the history doesn't exist — a chart path made unreachable by a missing binding. The metric-detail siblings pass priors correctly (AtriaOverviewSections.swift:8893-8902 `priorPoints: config.prior, overlays: expandedChartOverlays`). The Edit-chart sheet on this path likewise renders "No sibling metrics have enough saved data to overlay here yet" (AtriaGraphGrammar.swift:510) because `overlays` is never wired, blaming data for a plumbing gap.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Pass `priorPoints: prepared.previousSeries.map { AtriaDetailChartPoint(day: $0.date, value: $0.value, tint: metric.tint) }` (already time-shifted onto the current window) and `comparisonPeriodNoun: range.narrativeLabel`; optionally wire the other two metrics' series as overlays to match the metric-detail expand.
confirmed.why: AtriaTrendChart.swift:215-220 passes no priorPoints/overlays; compareAvailability then computes previousPeriodCount=0, failing minimumEvidenceMet (AtriaGraphGrammar.swift:114-116), so the sheet shows 'Nothing to compare against yet' (373) / 'Not enough saved history before this window yet' (99) — while the same card draws the dashed prior ghost under the identical max(3, count/2) gate (showGhost, 562-564). The expand button is a real production affordance (94-102), and the metric-detail sibling wires priors+overlays correctly (AtriaOverviewSections.swift:8897-8900). The Edit sheet's 'No sibling metrics' copy (AtriaGraphGrammar.swift:510) likewise blames data for the unwired overlays parameter. No documented rationale for the omission.

confirmed.title: Weekly-report recovery chart bridges missed days with its line, contradicting its own honesty comment
confirmed.evidence: AtriaOverviewSections.swift:5348-5349 promises `/// Week recovery sparkline ... only real recovery days plot -- a nil day is a gap in the dots, never invented.` but the chart at 5363-5368 draws `ForEach(points, id: \.day) { LineMark(x: .value("Day", point.day, unit: .day), y: .value("Recovery", point.recovery)).interpolationMethod(.linear) }` — one implicit continuous series with no `contiguousDayRuns()` split. `weekRecoveryPoints` (5352-5357) compactMaps nil-recovery days OUT, so a week of Mon/Wed/Sat recoveries renders dots with a straight LINE drawn across Tue and Thu-Fri: the gap exists only "in the dots" while the line invents the missing days. Violates "lines break at day gaps"; the inspector payload right below (5389-5402) even captions it "Recorded recovery days only".
confirmed.suggestedFix: Convert points to AtriaDetailChartPoint (or add a tuple-based run splitter) and iterate contiguous day-runs with per-run `series:` ids, as AtriaStrainRecoveryComboChart and AtriaPreparedMetricChart do.
confirmed.why: weekRecoveryPoints compactMaps nil-recovery days out (AtriaOverviewSections.swift:5352-5357); the LineMark at 5364-5368 has no series: id and no run split, so the implicit single series draws straight across missing days — contradicting the comment at 5348-5349 ('a nil day is a gap in the dots, never invented') and the inspector subtitle 'Recorded recovery days only' (5392). Rendered in the production weekly-report sheet whenever >=2 recovery days exist (5241-5242). Violates the lines-break-at-day-gaps rule; no counter-rationale found.

confirmed.title: Compact Trends card: current line and prior-period ghost both interpolate across day gaps
confirmed.evidence: AtriaTrendChart.swift:473-479 draws the current series as one unbroken run: `LineMark(x: .value("Date", sample.date), y: .value(metric.shortLabel, sample.value)).interpolationMethod(.linear)` inside `ForEach(prepared.series)` with no per-run `series:` id; the ghost overlay at 445-456 does the same with fixed `series: .value("Series", "prior")`. The card plots ONE point per civil day (comment at 21-22, and 235: "Days without a value are simply absent"), so a skipped wear night becomes a straight fabricated segment. Every other daily-bucketed chart in the app now breaks at gaps via `contiguousDayRuns()` (AtriaOverviewSections.swift:10831, AtriaStrainRecoveryComboChart.swift:102-116, AtriaAboutMetricSheet.swift:367-370) — this Vitals-tab card and the session-insights RestingTrendChart (Insights.swift:603-608, same single-series `.linear` pattern) are the remaining bridging surfaces.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Split prepared.series (and previousSeries) into contiguous day-runs and feed the run id into `series:` for both LineMarks; RestingTrendChart in Insights.swift needs the same treatment.
confirmed.why: The card plots one point per civil day (AtriaTrendChart.swift:20-21) and prepareSeries skips valueless days (279-288); the current series (473-479, no series id) and the ghost (445-457, fixed 'prior' id) both use .linear with no contiguousDayRuns split, so a skipped wear night becomes a fabricated straight segment. Production surface via AtriaVitalsCollectionSections.swift:170. Caveat: the cited Insights.swift:603-608 RestingTrendChart is code-true but plots per-SESSION points, not day buckets, so the day-gap rule fits it less cleanly; the primary trend-card claim stands regardless.

confirmed.title: Heart-rate timeline draws a continuous line across collection gaps while every sibling monitor chart segments them
confirmed.evidence: AtriaHeartRateAxisChart (AtriaVitalsCollectionSections.swift:4911-4920) draws raw samples as one unbroken series: `ForEach(points) { AreaMark(...).interpolationMethod(.linear) ... LineMark(x: .value("Time", point.t), y: .value("BPM", point.bpm)).interpolationMethod(.linear) }` — no gap segmentation; the smoothed path (4898-4909) is worse: empty buckets are dropped via compactMap (4087-4092) and the average line then connects straight across them. This chart backs the Vitals "Heart-rate timeline · Last 6 hr" card (3985) and the workout HR trace (AtriaActivityMonitor.swift:1924), so two hours with the strap off render as a confident straight red line with area fill under it. The app's own monitor idiom explicitly forbids this: the stress strip splits `series: .value("Segment", point.segment)` where "A gap longer than 5 minutes bumps `segment` ... so the strip leaves a real blank instead of interpolating across a stretch the strap wasn't read (the honesty contract)" (AtriaHealthScreen.swift:1769-1772, 1794-1805), and the stress timeline/workout stress trace caption "blanks are collection gaps" (AtriaActivityMonitor.swift:941-943, AtriaStressDetailView.swift:431). Same screens, sibling metric, opposite honesty.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Apply the stress-strip segmenting rule to HR: bump a segment id when consecutive samples (or bucket centers) are more than N minutes apart and pass it to `series:` on both the LineMark and AreaMark.
confirmed.why: Both modes of AtriaHeartRateAxisChart bridge gaps: raw points (AtriaVitalsCollectionSections.swift:4911-4920) and smoothed buckets (4898-4909, with empty buckets dropped via compactMap at 4087-4092) are single-series .linear with no segmentation anywhere in the AtriaHeartRateChartSeries pipeline. Backs the production Vitals 'Heart-rate timeline · Last 6 hr' card (3985) and the workout HR trace (AtriaActivityMonitor.swift:1924). Sibling stress charts on the same screens document the segment-at-gaps honesty contract (AtriaHealthScreen.swift:1769-1772; AtriaActivityMonitor.swift:941-943). No documented decision to bridge.

confirmed.title: Activity stress monitor colors its latest-point dot and pins band labels at integer boundaries that are not the monitor's real band bounds
confirmed.evidence: AtriaActivityMonitor.swift:880-886 hard-codes `let stressPointColor: (Double) -> Color = { score in switch score { case ..<1.0: return Metrics.electricStrain; case ..<2.0: return Metrics.electricGreen; default: return Metrics.electricStress } }` and the y-axis at 912-921 pins `["Calm", "Low", "Med", "High"]` at values 0/1/2/3. The monitor's actual band boundaries on the plotted 0-3 score scale are 0.60 / 1.35 / 2.16 (AtriaStressMonitor.swift:154-156 `calmUpperBound = 0.20`, `lowUpperBound = 0.45`, `mediumUpperBound = 0.72`, x3 per AtriaStressDetailReading `score: historyPoint.activation * 3`), and the stress detail view already uses the real bound for its elevated evidence (`elevatedThresholdScore = AtriaStressMonitor.lowUpperBound * 3` = 1.35, AtriaStressDetailView.swift:131). Failure: a reading of 1.2 is level LOW — the value readout beside the chart tints yellow via `stressMonitorStore.state.level?.tint` (865; tints at AtriaStressMonitor.swift:33-38) — while the latest-point dot at 903-907 paints it the medium green; at 2.1 the model says medium (orange pill) while the axis places it above the "Med" label heading for "High". The graph and the state pill on the same card disagree about which band the same number is in.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Derive the dot color from AtriaStressMonitor.band(score/3) (or the level tint mapping) and either place band labels at the real boundary values or label regions rather than integer ticks.
confirmed.why: All facts verified: bounds 0.20/0.45/0.72 activation (AtriaStressMonitor.swift:154-156) x3 via score=activation*3 (AtriaStressDetailView.swift:21) give real plotted bounds 0.60/1.35/2.16; the detail view uses the real 1.35 threshold (131). The dot buckets at 1.0/2.0 (AtriaActivityMonitor.swift:880-886) match neither the model bands nor the line gradient's geometry, so a 1.2 Low reading (yellow pill via level.tint, AtriaStressMonitor.swift:33-38) gets an electricGreen dot; the axis pins Calm/Low/Med/High at 0/1/2/3 (912-921) so a High 2.5 plots below 'High' and a Low 0.7 below 'Low'. Only the line gradient is documented as deliberate (868-873) — the dot buckets and integer labels are not. Nuance: the finding's 2.1 example is its weakest case (2.1 IS medium and sits just above 'Med'); the contradiction is cleanest in the 0.60-1.0 and 2.16-3.0 sub-ranges, and the colored dot also literally violates 'only the line carries range color'.

confirmed.title: No-value token drift: em-dash "—" instead of the canonical "--" on History rows, day sheet, and stress gauge
confirmed.evidence: The canonical not-computable token is `static let noValue = "--"` (AtriaMetricConfidencePresentation.swift:76), and the house rule is numeral-or-"--". But AtriaHistorySection.swift:561 renders `Text(day.strain.map { "\(AtriaMetricFormat.strain($0)) strain" } ?? "—")` on every history day row, and the day sheet repeats it at 1419 (`value: day.recovery.map { "\($0)%" } ?? "—"`) and 1431 (`value: day.rhrInt.map { "\($0) bpm" } ?? "—"`); the stress hero gauge does the same at AtriaStressDetailView.swift:651 (`score?.formatted(...) ?? "—"`). The very file that defines pending-value detection has to special-case the drift: AtriaOverviewSections.swift:11434 `if v.isEmpty || v == "—" || v == "--" { return true }`. Two vocabularies for one state, sitting beside sibling surfaces that use "--" (e.g. AtriaOverviewSections.swift:4119, 4234).
confirmed.suggestedFix: Replace the em-dash fallbacks on user-facing metric value slots with AtriaMetricConfidencePresentation.noValue ("--"); leave debug/BLE-internal strings alone.
confirmed.why: Canonical token is noValue = "--" (AtriaMetricConfidencePresentation.swift:76, with rule doc at line 16). Em-dash renders on production surfaces at AtriaHistorySection.swift:561 (strain row), 1419 (recovery), 1431 (RHR) and AtriaStressDetailView.swift:651 (hero scoreText). Both pending-value detectors special-case the drift (trimmed == "\u{2014}" at AtriaMetricConfidencePresentation.swift:110; AtriaOverviewSections.swift:11434), proving the codebase treats em-dash as tolerated legacy, not a sanctioned second vocabulary. Distinct from the excluded ASCII ' -- ' recommendation-copy item. Low severity as claimed.

confirmed.title: Monthly report feature is unreachable — its only presenter lives in a never-mounted view
confirmed.evidence: The only presentation of the monthly report in the entire app is line 3125: `.sheet(isPresented: $showMonthlyReport) { AtriaMonthlyReportSheet(report: monthlyReportHighlight ?? MonthlyReport(rollups: dailyRollupHistory))`, and the only setter is line 3012 `showMonthlyReport = true` (behind the Week/Month `AtriaTextSelector(items: [AtriaReportPeriod.week, .month]...)` at 2994). All of this is inside `struct AtriaOverviewReadinessSection` (line 2776), which is mounted only via `AtriaOverviewReadinessSectionHost` (1989), which is mounted only at lines 421 and 1596 — both inside the `AtriaOverviewTabContent` tree (line 125), which has ZERO instantiations anywhere in the app. The live Overview mounts `AtriaTodayScreen` (AtriaHomeView.swift:4981), which presents only `AtriaWeeklyReportSheet` (AtriaTodayScreen.swift:328-329). So `AtriaMonthlyReportSheet` (5507), `AtriaMonthlyReportHighlightRow` (5458), and the whole `MonthlyReport` UI are dead: a user can never see a monthly report, while the model keeps being computed in the (dead) readiness projection (2736).
confirmed.suggestedFix: Give the monthly report a live entry point (e.g., the Today weekly-plan card's report sheet gains the Week/Month selector, or a row on the Vitals/Health screen), or delete the monthly-report UI deliberately.
confirmed.why: REACHABLE? No — AtriaOverviewTabContent (AtriaOverviewSections.swift:125) has zero instantiations in Atria, AtriaWidget, or AtriaShared; both AtriaOverviewReadinessSectionHost mounts (421 via AtriaDisconnectedOverviewHost@211, 1596 via AtriaOverviewLeadingSection@1554 <- sole mount at 700 <- hosts at 229/254/287) sit inside that dead root, and no DEBUG fixture or #Preview mounts it. TRUE? Yes — AtriaMonthlyReportSheet is presented only at line 3126; the live Overview is AtriaTodayScreen (AtriaHomeView.swift:4980) which presents only AtriaWeeklyReportSheet (AtriaTodayScreen.swift:328-332), with zero Monthly references in that file; MonthlyReport's only compute site (2736) is inside AtriaOverviewReadinessProjectionStore, instantiated only at 2065 in the dead host. DELIBERATE? No comment or doc marks the monthly report as deferred/removed — nothing in docs/, product-decisions memory, or nearby comments. A weekly report is user-visible while the fully-built monthly report can never be seen.

confirmed.title: Behavior-insights engine output is computed forever but has no live UI; the live 'Insights' tile shows highlights instead
confirmed.evidence: Sessions.swift:6533 `@Published private(set) var behaviorInsights: [AtriaInsight] = []` is recomputed on the utility queue on every behavior recompute (13711 `let insights = SessionStore.deriveInsights(from: summaries)` → 13723 `self.behaviorInsights = insights`), snapshot-persisted/restored (9974, 10104), and has its own recompute component (10842 `.behaviorInsights`). Its ONLY renderer is `AtriaInsightsCard` (AtriaOverviewSections.swift:14308), instantiated solely at 14299 inside `AtriaInsightsCardHost` (14295) — which has zero mounts (only reachable from the dead readiness section's `insightsCard` Button at 4254, itself dead).
